summary.text: Emily Alvarado is a Democratic member of the Washington State Senate from District 34, which she has represented since January 21, 2025, and she is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She is an attorney whose career has focused on housing policy.

paragraphs.text: Alvarado earned a B.A. in American studies from Scripps College in 2003 and a J.D. from the University of Washington School of Law in 2009.

Her career experience includes working as an attorney, as policy director of the Housing Development Consortium of Seattle, as director of policy and outreach for Pittsburgh United, as director of the City of Seattle's Office of Housing, and as vice president and Pacific Northwest market leader for Enterprise Community Partners.
Alvarado represented House District 34-Position 1 from 2023 to 2025, succeeding Eileen Cody (D), and then succeeded Joe Nguyen (D) in the Senate.
In the 2023-2024 session she was vice chair of the Housing and House Local Government committees and served on the Capital Budget Committee.
No other candidate is listed for the November ballot.
